messages:
marta: Hi team — our private onprem meter shows ~1.20M tokens for 2026-03-15 but our internal audit ledger only records ~1.07M. ~12% discrepancy. Running agent v2.3.1 on host onprem-01. Can you escalate?

andrea-support: Thanks Marta — escalating. Can you paste agent id + any relevant logs and exact time window? Also which collector region?

marta: agent_id=9f3a, host=onprem-01, window=2026-03-15T00:00:00Z..2026-03-15T23:59:59Z. Collector is vpc-eu-west-2. Will paste logs in a sec.

kevin-eng: looping infra/eng. @andrea-support pls confirm if there were any planned restarts / kube-drain around that date. Also any network blips?

andrea-support: Customer said there was an automated node drain 03:12Z and agent restarted ~03:15Z. They also saw a transient network partition to the collector for ~6–10s.

sasha-infra: checking metrics — there is a heartbeat gap 03:10Z–03:18Z. agent buffered_count spikes to ~180k then flushes. Looks suspiciously like an offline flush + re-send. Need logs to confirm if batches were re-applied.

marta: Logs (excerpt):
```
[2026-03-15T03:14:59Z] INFO  onprem-meter flush_batch id=abc123 seq_start=100001 seq_end=100500 count=500
[2026-03-15T03:15:01Z] WARN  onprem-meter ack_timeout batch=abc123 retrying
[2026-03-15T03:15:07Z] INFO  onprem-meter reapplied batch id=abc123 seq_start=100001 seq_end=100500
[2026-03-15T03:15:08Z] INFO  collector recv_batch id=abc123 seq_start=100001 seq_end=100500
```
Audit (their ledger) only shows that seq range once. Meter (what we bill) contains both entries.

kevin-eng: that log pattern (reapplied batch) + collector recv shortly after is classic ack-loss -> re-send. Why would meter double-count? We should dedupe on seq_id. Any chance seq header missing/changed on this agent build?

sasha-infra: agent v2.3.1 sometimes omitted the seq-id header on retransmit if the network layer retried at socket level. Collector earlier had a fallback match by timestamp when seq header missing — this can double-count when two identical batches arrive separated by ~8s. Also host NTP offset was non-zero — I see +6.7s skew that drifted to +10s in that window. Combined with timestamp matching, duplicates pass through.

andrea-support: Customer asks: will they be charged for the duplicate tokens? We need reconciliation and a credit if meter overcounted.

kevin-eng: Proposed next steps: 1) Run a reconcile job that dedupes meter by seq ranges for agent 9f3a for the day 2026-03-15 and produce a reconciled token count (I can run this). 2) Patch collector to prefer seq_id matching and ignore timestamp fallback (hotfix) — low-risk config toggle `enable_strict_seq=true`. 3) Recommend customer upgrade to v2.4.0 which always sets seq header and adds stronger idempotency. 4) Provide billing credit after reconciliation. ETA: reconcile + report in ~6 hours.

marta: Thanks — can you share repro steps so we can validate on our side? We prefer not to do agent upgrade during business hours.

sasha-infra: Repro steps (short): create a controlled network blackout ~8–12s, let agent buffer batches, then reply/flush with retransmit. On collector side run `enable_strict_seq=false` to mimic old fallback. Patch suggestion: collector should persist last_seen_seq per agent and drop overlapping ranges. Logs to collect: `journalctl -u onprem-meter -o short-iso --since '2026-03-15 02:50' --until '2026-03-15 04:00'` and collector logs around 03:14–03:16Z. Workaround (no agent restart): flip `enable_strict_seq=true` on collector to stop timestamp-based matching.

andrea-support: I'll coordinate with billing for provisional credit once the reconcile run completes and we verify duplicates. @kevin-eng please attach the reconciliation CSV when done.

marta: Appreciate the quick follow-up. One question — will enabling `enable_strict_seq` risk dropping legit late arrivals? We want minimal data loss.

sasha-infra: Good question — strict mode only uses explicit seq ids and will accept late arrivals if they have higher seq_end than last_seen. It only rejects overlapping seq ranges. For safety we can run reconcile first then flip the flag during low traffic.

kevin-eng: Agreed. I'll start the reconcile now and post results in this thread.

andrea-support: Thanks all. @marta we'll keep you updated. :white_check_mark:
